name: Saint John Gualbert
history: A young Florentine nobleman who, on Good Friday, met the man who had killed his brother and, when the man begged for mercy with his arms outstretched like a cross, spared him. Tradition holds that the crucifix in the church where he then prayed bowed its head to him. He became a monk and founded the abbey of Vallombrosa.
life: John Gualbert was bound by the code of his class to avenge his brother’s murder. Riding into Florence with armed men on Good Friday, he came upon the killer in a narrow way where neither could pass. The man fell to his knees and stretched out his arms, and John, remembering Christ who forgave on that day, put up his sword and embraced him. He went into the church of San Miniato to pray, and the crucifix, as tradition tells it, bowed to him. He became a Benedictine monk there, but left when a new abbot bought his office. After a time at Camaldoli he founded his own community in the forested valley of Vallombrosa, east of Florence, under a strict Benedictine rule. He fought simony fearlessly and cared for the poor in famine. He died in 1073 and was canonised in 1193. Pius XII named him patron of foresters.
prayerTo: Saint John Gualbert, you had every right by the world’s standards to take revenge, and on Good Friday you chose mercy. Pray for all who have been gravely wronged, for those who long for revenge, and for me, that I may forgive as Christ forgave me, from the cross. Amen.
penance: Pray for someone who has hurt you, by name, and do them some small good today if you can. Spend a few minutes before a crucifix.
meditation: The man who killed his brother held out his arms like a cross, and John saw Christ in him. Whose outstretched arms have you ignored?
prayer: May the intercession of the blessed Abbot Joánnis Gualbérti, commend us to You, O Lord, so that through his merits we may obtain that which we cannot accomplish by our own. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
